newsitem.title: DUBAI: Air cargo business out of Dubai slips off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo business out of Dubai slips off peaks.

text.p: Business in the Dubai air cargo market slowed in May and early June, with rates moving off their April highs, a Reuters survey shows.
Rates to central Europe and the United States have ebbed in the past six weeks after peaking in April, while only rates to Nairobi gained ground.
"The market has been through a low period in the last month. In general, things should improve this month," said EVA Air cargo manager Leonard Thyagarajan.
"May was very slow. Airlines were desperately looking for cargo," said one airline manager.
Demand from Europe, which had been buoyant thanks to summer fashion shipments after the slow start to the year, had eased.
Trade to the U.S. was also seen slightly weaker but some agents reported more regular garment shipments from Muscat in neighbouring Oman transiting Dubai and destined for New York.
The average rate on shipments to London Heathrow at 4.15 dirhams per kg was down from 4.20 dirhams at the end of April. Similarly, the average rate to Frankfurt was down at 4.15 dirhams.
To the United States, the average to JFK was 6.40 dirhams from 6.50 a kg six weeks ago, and the rate to Los Angeles was at 7.45 dirhams from an average 7.60 dirhams.

"Rates to the United States have been very low and some have been offering as low as 4.75 to JFK via transhipment in the Gulf and 4.80 to five dirhams to Los Angeles and the West coast," one airline executive said.

Despite the lower volume moving to the United States, one agent reported good tonnages of textile exports to Canada. "We recently had eight tonnes of garments to Montreal," he said, adding rates charged on these heavyweight shipments were around 6.70 dirhams a kg.
Smaller shipments, of 100 kg plus, would cost about 7.30 dirhams per kg, the executive said.

Air cargo operators said business to east Africa was brisk. "Business is good, most of it is into Nairobi, but there is also some going to Lagos and Dar es Salaam. It is mainly (car and machinery) spare parts," he said.
Reflecting this strength, the average rate to Nairobi moved up to 4.30 from 4.15 dirhams a kg six weeks ago.
On the usually quiet Far Eastern routes, rates were steady.

Agents and airlines said shipments of perishables from Oman to the Far East, mostly via Dubai, had slowed with the start of the Arabian summer. "Vegetables from Oman have dried up and fish is only moving in small quantities," said one.
The average rate to Singapore and Hong Kong was at four dirhams a kg.
Forwarders and shippers said all airlines operating out of Dubai had scrapped fuel surcharges, which had been applied since last November. -- Dubai newsroom +9714-626990
